It started with a QQ Music HD bug on AxionOS. After switching away from the app, the audio would cut out while the progress bar kept moving. Pausing and resuming picked up from the point where the sound had stopped. Android’s cached-app freezer was suspending the player in the background.

The first version, QQ Music Relay, was a small tool for that one player. Its Home screen shortcut bound to QQ Music HD’s playback service before opening the app, keeping the player responsive in the background. It later added a connection notification and an action to exit the player.

It became Media Service Relay when the same approach was made available to other compatible apps. Saved profiles, custom shortcuts, logs, and a tablet layout came next. The connection cards can now show live audio spectra and control playback through the app’s media session.
Added a playback controls switch and widened the spectrum area so longer labels fit.
